cells.tense: You are here with your hands already open, and the thing is finished.
cells.act: care for it with fresh hands and see what it needs
cells.ask: Take a duty you still carry for your people — a role, a habit of turning up — and meet it as if for the first time. Notice what it wants from you now.
cells.core:
When something here has run its course, you can set it down and keep your footing. That is rare. Most keep the role long after the reason for it ended, because setting it down looks like losing. You finish from a full place, not a defeated one, and the ones you belong to get a version of you that is here because you chose it — not because you forgot to put something down.

The next thing this balance feeds is smaller than it looks. Take a duty you still carry — a role, a habit of turning up — and meet it as if for the first time. What does it want now? Not what it wanted when you took it on. You may find it wants less than you have been giving, or something different. Both are information. Tend it, and watch.

cells.tense: The next handover, the next goodbye, is already being rehearsed before anything has finished.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Take a role you still hold. Put the facts on paper — what is done, what is left, who waits on what. Follow the page where it goes.
cells.core:
Endings are being prepared for before the things have ended. You are already handing over the role, already closing the chapter, already thinking about who takes this on after you — and the place you are standing in is getting less of you than it should. Leaving early feels like wisdom. Mostly it is how a person avoids the unglamorous middle, where nothing is complete and nothing can be set down yet.

Take a role you still hold and put the facts on paper. What is done. What is left. Who waits on what. Follow the page where it goes. It will tell you whether this is finished or merely uncomfortable. Only one of those is a reason to let go.

cells.tense: The handover happened, the role ended, and you are standing at a door you already walked through.
cells.ask: Give this place one practice your people will still be keeping a year from now — a meal, a call, a mark on a certain day — and keep it going.
cells.core:
You stepped back from something here — a role, a group, a place you used to belong — and you have not picked anything up since. That stepping back was real, and it was right, and a door closed behind you that you are still at. Meantime the others have gone on to the next thing, and you watch them carry it, and nothing in your hands is holding anything.

Give this place one practice your people will still be keeping a year from now. A meal, a call, a small mark on a certain day — and you keep it going. Small enough to hold. Built to last. This is not a statement. It is one stone set somewhere it will still be, and it is how a person rejoins the room they left.
cells.sheetLine: The door closed behind you and you are still at it.

cells.tense: You keep this place running, and if anybody asked, you would say you just show up like the rest.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Find a piece of this place that only works because you keep it going, and tend it, watching how it actually grows instead of holding it alive from memory.
cells.core:
You hold something here together that no one has named. The way things are done, the thing everybody assumes will happen, the reason the group still knows what it is — a good part of that is you, ongoing, and the story you tell has you as simply among the people who turn up. Nobody corrects you, because from outside it looks like it runs itself.

Find a piece of this place that only works because you keep it going, and tend it. Watch how it grows, instead of holding it alive from memory. You may find it has been drawing on you in ways you stopped noticing. Start something in it that is yours — a version only you would make — and the thing keeps going with your fingerprints in it.
